items.title: LLM Batch APIs: The Half-Price Lane Nobody Budgets
items.why_it_matters: LLM providers offer up to 50% discounts for API requests that can wait up to 24 hours to execute. Since your AI-ingest tool runs on a daily schedule to filter news, you do not need real-time responses, and switching to batch processing will cut your API bill in half. This week, modify your AI-ingest backend script to bundle your daily candidate articles and send them to Anthropic's Message Batches API instead of making individual live calls.

items.title: Maximizing the value of your Claude Code sessions
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic released a guide on optimizing Claude Code sessions to prevent runaway token usage and keep costs low. Since you use Claude Code daily, managing your session context prevents the tool from sending your entire git history and workspace files on every turn, saving you money and keeping responses fast. This week, run `claude compact` in your terminal during a long coding session to clear out old message history while keeping the essential context of your current task.

items.title: Show HN: Remarc – contextual feedback for coding agents via MCP
items.why_it_matters: Remarc is a new open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets you give precise, contextual feedback to coding agents instead of typing out long, messy chat explanations. If you are directing Claude to build your Next.js frontend, you can use this to visually point out exactly what needs to change. This week, install Remarc via MCP and use it to highlight a specific UI bug or hover-state issue on your AI-ingest frontend so Claude can fix it instantly.

items.title: Show HN: Mole – Deep research agent for your terminal
items.why_it_matters: Mole is a new open-source terminal-based deep research agent that enforces strict budget limits and verifies its sources, keeping your data local. This is useful when you need to research new APIs or libraries for your projects without risking runaway API costs or hallucinated documentation. This week, install Mole via npm and run a quick research query on Supabase's latest real-time features to see how you can integrate them into your app.

items.title: Show HN: Control Claude Code, Codex, Pi and Gemini CLI from Telegram
items.why_it_matters: Cliclaw is a lightweight CLI tool that lets you control Claude Code, Codex, and other LLMs directly from a Telegram chat. If you want to run quick code checks or trigger builds while away from your laptop, this bridges your mobile device to your terminal tools. This week, clone the repo, link it to a private Telegram bot, and try triggering a Git commit or a quick code explanation on your AI-ingest project from your phone.
